# Extract declination values and convert to decimal degrees
def declination_to_decimal(dec_str):
    # Format: degreeXX′YY″
    # Example: degree22′44″
    # Remove 'degree' and split by ′ and ″
    dec_str = dec_str.replace('degree', '').replace('′', ' ').replace('″', '')
    parts = dec_str.split()
    degrees = float(parts[0])
    minutes = float(parts[1]) if len(parts) > 1 else 0
    seconds = float(parts[2]) if len(parts) > 2 else 0
    return degrees + minutes/60 + seconds/3600

# Apply conversion
df['declination_decimal'] = df['declination ( j2000 )'].apply(declination_to_decimal)

# Get the two highest declination values
top_two_declinations = df['declination_decimal'].nlargest(2).values

# Check if any globular cluster has the second highest declination
second_highest = top_two_declinations[1] if len(top_two_declinations) > 1 else None
globular_clusters = df[df['object type'] == 'globular cluster']
has_second_highest = any(globular_clusters['declination_decimal'] == second_highest)

answer = has_second_highest
